outcome: incidence of urological injuries (bladder, ureteric, combined)
timing of detection of urological injuries (intraoperative, early postoperative ≤7 days, late postoperative >7 days)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 15,697 patients who underwent either gynecologic surgeries (6150 procedures) or lower segment cesarean sections (9547 procedures) at a tertiary care center.
finding: Urological injuries occurred in 0.27% of procedures, with most (76.7%) detected intraoperatively, and early recognition facilitated effective management leading to favorable outcomes and a mean hospital stay of four to 12 days.
mod_finding: Bladder injuries were slightly more frequent during obstetric procedures (cesarean sections) (0.23%) compared to gynecologic procedures (0.19%).
followup_time: Injury detection was classified as early (≤7 days) or late (>7 days) post-procedure, with mean hospital stay ranging from four to 12 days for those with injuries.
